question.prompt: How many nonnegative integers can be written in the form \[a_7\cdot3^7+a_6\cdot3^6+a_5\cdot3^5\]\[+a_4\cdot3^4+a_3\cdot3^3+a_2\cdot3^2\]\[+a_1\cdot3^1+a_0\cdot3^0,\] where \(a_i\in \{-1,0,1\}\) for \(0\le i \le 7?\)

solutions.title: Shift to base three and pair opposite values
solutions.explanation:
Adding \(1\) to each coefficient changes the allowed coefficients into the ordinary base \(3\) digits \(0,1,2\). This lets us count distinct values, rather than just coefficient choices.

Let \(S\) contain all integers of the given form, including negative ones, and put
\[
K=1+3+3^2+\cdots+3^7.
\]
For an allowed sum \(N\), set \(b_i=a_i+1\). Then
\[
N+K=\sum_{i=0}^{7}b_i3^i,
\qquad b_i\in\{0,1,2\}.
\]
The right side is an ordinary base \(3\) expansion with eight digit positions, allowing leading zeros. Every integer from \(0\) through \(3^8-1\) has exactly one such expansion. Conversely, subtracting \(1\) from each digit recovers allowed coefficients \(a_i\). Thus the \(3^8\) coefficient choices give \(3^8=6561\) distinct integers in \(S\).

Negating every coefficient changes \(N\) into \(-N\), so the nonzero values pair into one positive and one negative value. Zero is also represented, by taking every coefficient to be zero. Therefore the number of nonnegative values is
\[
1+\frac{6561-1}{2}=\boxed{3281},
\]
choice \(\text{D}\).
